applicant_utility.summary: This is a 100% tuition scholarship for citizens of Bangladesh, Bhutan, Mauritius, Myanmar and Nepal who apply to a Deakin coursework degree through an authorised Deakin agent in their own region, with strong academic results (85% in Year 12, a GCSE/A Level score of 10, IBDP 32, or 80% in an undergraduate degree). The award pays all course tuition and includes compulsory participation in the Vice-Chancellor's Professional Excellence Program, but flights, visa, insurance, accommodation and daily living costs remain entirely on you. One caution before you plan around it: the official scholarship page is currently offline and Deakin's live scholarships hub no longer features this South Asia variant, so confirm with the Deakin South Asia office (sa-info@deakin.edu.au) that it still runs for your intake.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-achieving school leavers and strong undergraduate performers from Bangladesh, Bhutan, Mauritius, Myanmar or Nepal who can apply through an in-region Deakin agent and want 100% tuition covered in Australia.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm with the Deakin South Asia office (sa-info@deakin.edu.au) that the South Asia 100% scholarship is still offered for your intended intake
Engage a Deakin authorised agent in your country early - applying directly to Deakin does not meet the published route
Prepare certified academic transcripts and award certificates, passport and English proficiency evidence for the course application
Draft the 300-word personal statement in your own voice, covering your motivation, extracurricular or paid/voluntary experience, and ambassador qualities
Brief two referees so they can speak specifically to community engagement and/or leadership, and confirm their contact details
common_rejection_risks: Applying directly to Deakin instead of through a Deakin authorised agent based in the same region, which fails the published eligibility route
Not residing in one of the five eligible countries at the time of application, or holding citizenship outside the list
Academic results below the published thresholds; meeting the minimum is not a guarantee and competition for a small number of awards is strong
A generic or ghost-written personal statement that does not reflect your own voice
Applying to the Doctor of Medicine (H911), which is explicitly excluded
Failing to accept the terms and conditions in the offer acceptance form, on which the scholarship is conditional
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Everything except tuition: return airfares, student visa and overseas health cover, on-campus or rented accommodation (priority access is at your own cost), food, transport and day-to-day living costs in Australia.
document_audit: The 300-word personal statement must be in your own words and specifically address why Deakin, your extracurricular or work experience, and your ambassador potential - recycled statements are easy to spot
Referees must be able to comment on community engagement and/or leadership, so give them the scholarship context before they write
Academic transcripts must accompany the course application; Deakin's international guidance requires certified copies, and non-English documents need certified translation
Be prepared for a possible interview if you are shortlisted
